transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well, I hope it's okay that I came in. I mean, I'm sure you see people with much worse problems, but... I guess I've just been a little jumpy lately at work. I do maintenance and repair, so it's a loud job, you know? But recently, if a breaker snaps or someone drops a wrench, or even if one of the guys just walks up behind me when I'm not looking, I just... I jump out of my skin. And my heart will just keep hammering away for a long time, even after everyone else has gone back to work. I know it's probably nothing, just stress or something, but my boss suggested I talk to someone. Is that... does that make sense for why I'd be here?
Have you noticed yourself feeling more anxious or worried about things in general, even when there's no specific loud noise or sudden event happening?

Um, no, not really. I mean... I hope that's okay to say. I don't want to make it sound like I'm just complaining about everything, you know? If things are quiet and I'm just doing my work, I'm usually fine. I don't really sit around worrying about things out of nowhere. It's really just... just when something catches me off guard, like I said. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you're not at work and in a calm environment, do you ever feel a constant sense of worry or tension that doesn't seem to go away, even when there's nothing specific to be concerned about?

Um... no, not really. I hope it's alright that I keep saying no to that. I really don't want you to think I'm wasting your time or being difficult or anything. But... yeah, if I'm just at home, you know, sitting in my living room and it's quiet, I'm usually okay. I don't really have that constant worry hanging over me if nothing's going on. I just try to relax. Am I... is it okay that I don't have that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
When you're startled by a sudden noise or someone surprising you, does it ever feel like you're having a panic attack, with symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling like you can't breathe?

Um, well... I wouldn't call it a panic attack, really. I mean, I don't want to overstate it or sound dramatic. My heart definitely beats fast, like I mentioned before, but... I don't think I stop breathing or anything like that. It's just a really strong jolt, you know? Like I just need a minute to catch my breath and settle down, but I'm not... I'm not totally losing control or anything. I hope that's the right way to explain it. I just don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself getting startled easily or being on edge even in places other than work, like at home or when you're out running errands?

Um... yeah, it happens other places too, not just at work. I mean, the reason I finally decided to come see you... and I really hope this isn't a silly reason to be here... is that I just can't stop jumping out of my skin. Like, if a breaker snaps on a job, or somebody drops a wrench, or even just if my wife comes up behind me in the kitchen when I'm not expecting it... I just jump. And then my heart just keeps hammering and hammering for a long time, way after everyone else has already moved on and forgotten about it. It's really embarrassing, honestly. I try to hide it, but... it's hard. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places or situations because you're worried about being startled or having that strong reaction again?

Um... yeah, I guess I do avoid some things. I really hope it doesn't make me sound like I'm slacking off at work or anything, I promise I'm a hard worker. But... I do make excuses sometimes to not go near certain panels or breakers, or even specific job sites. And... I try really hard not to even talk about that day. I just... I know if I get too close to it, or if I start thinking about it, it just starts playing in my head and I can't shut it off. I don't want to be difficult on the job, I really don't, I just... I have to stay away from it so I don't freak out. I hope you understand why I do that. Is it okay that I avoid those things?
Has something happened to you recently, or in the past, that was really scary or traumatic, especially related to a loud noise or a sudden event?

Um... well, yes. I hope it's okay to talk about work again, I know I keep bringing it up. But... there was this accident on a retrofit job. An arc-flash. It was... it was pretty bad. Really loud, really bright. I don't want to make it sound like I'm traumatized or anything dramatic, it's just part of the job sometimes, you know? But ever since that happened... which was about a year and a month ago now... that's when all this started. I really tried to just shake it off and keep working, I promise I did. I didn't want to be a bother to anyone. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
Since the arc-flash incident, have you found yourself re-living the event through sudden, intrusive memories or flashbacks, where it feels like you’re right back in the moment it happened?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it, but... yeah. It happens when I'm not even thinking about work. Like, I could just be loading tools into the back of the truck, minding my own business, and then... out of nowhere, I'll just see that bright flash right in my head. Or... or I'll hear the new trainee yelling. And it just... it knocks me sideways. For a second, it feels exactly like I'm right back there and it's happening all over again. I try to snap out of it quick so nobody notices, but it's really jarring. I'm sorry if that sounds crazy. Is that... is that normal for someone who went through something like that?
Do you notice that you're generally more alert or watchful, even in safe or familiar places, like you're always on the lookout for something going wrong?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to pay attention to my surroundings, especially on a job site where things can be a little unpredictable, but I wouldn't say I'm always on edge or anything. I don't want you to think I'm paranoid or jumping at shadows all the time. I'm usually pretty relaxed when I'm at home or just hanging out. I hope that's the right answer. I'm just trying to be honest with you. Is it a bad thing if I'm not always on the lookout like that?
Since the arc-flash incident, have you found yourself feeling ongoing fear, anger, or guilt, even when you're not directly reminded of the event?

Um... I mean, I try to keep a positive attitude, I really do. I don't want to be one of those guys who just complains or brings everybody down. But... yeah. I guess I do feel like that a lot. 

I just... I walk around feeling mad, and... and really guilty, almost all the time. It's like I failed that kid, the trainee, and I just feel like everybody can see it on me, you know? Like it's written on my face. I try to hide it so I'm not a burden to my crew or my family, but it's just always there in the background. I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't let it get to me like this. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Since the arc-flash incident, have you had trouble sleeping or experienced nightmares that might be related to what happened?

Um... well, I really try to get a good night's rest so I'm fresh for work, you know? I don't want to be dragging on the job and making mistakes. But... I guess sleep hasn't been great lately. I hope it's not a big deal, I mean, everybody has trouble sleeping sometimes, right? 

But... yeah. Most nights, I just lay there for hours. It sounds stupid, but I find myself just... listening. Like I'm waiting to hear a pop or a buzzing sound coming from the walls. And then, when I finally do fall asleep... I don't know, I guess I do have some bad dreams. I'll wake up just completely soaked in sweat, like... like I'm right back on that job site again. I try to just wash my face and go back to bed so I don't bother my wife, but... it's hard. Is it okay that I'm struggling with that? I really am trying to get over it.
